text: 120 g of an organic compound that contains only carbon and hydrogen gives 330 g of $CO_{2}$ and 270 g of water on complete combustion. The percentage of carbon and hydrogen, respectively are
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$C_{x}H_{y}+\left (x+\frac{y}{4}\right )O_{2}\to xCO_{2}+\frac{y}{2}H_{2}O$

From the reaction,

Produced $CO_{2} = x$ mol

and produced $H_{2}O =$ $\frac{y}{2}$ mol

Given produced $CO_{2} = 330 g$

$\therefore$ moles of $CO_{2}$ $=\frac{330}{44}=\frac{30}{4}=x$

Also given produced $H_{2}O = 270 gm$

$\therefore$ Moles of $H_{2}O$ $=\frac{270}{18}=15=\frac{y}{2}$.

$\Rightarrow$ y = 30

$\therefore$ $x:y=\frac{30}{4}:30=1:4$

Formula of the compound = $(CH_{4})_{n}$

$\therefore$ Weight of C in $(CH_{4})_{n}$ = 12 n

Weight of H in $(CH_{4})_{n}$ = 4 n

$\therefore$ Weight ratio of C and H

= 12 n : 4 n

= 3 : 1

$\therefore$ % of C = $\frac{3}{4}$ $\times$ 100 = 75

and % of H = $\frac{1}{4}$ $\times$ 100 = 25
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Evening Shift

text:
The energy of one mole of photons of radiation of wavelength 300 nm is

 (Given : h = 6.63 $\times$ $10^{-34} J s, N_{A} = 6.02$ $\times$ $10^{23}$ mol$^{-1}, c = 3$ $\times$ $10^{8} m s^{-1})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Energy of one photon

$E=\frac{1240}{λ(nm)}eV$

$=\frac{1240}{300}$

$=4.1333eV$

$\therefore$ Energy of one mole of photon

$=4.1333\times 6.02\times 10^{23}eV$

$=4.1333\times 6.02\times 10^{23}\times 1.6\times 10^{-19}J$

$=\frac{4.1333\times 6.02\times 10^{23}\times 1.6\times 10^{-19}}{1000}kJ$

$=399kJ/mol$

 is, respectively
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Note : 

(1) [MATH$_$FAILED] Bond order $=\frac{1}{2}$ [$N_{b}$ $-$ $N_{a}$] 

$N_{b} =$ No of electrons in bonding molecular orbital 

$N_{a}$ $=$ No of electrons in anti bonding molecular orbital 

(2) $\, ~$ upto 14 electrons, molecular orbital configuration is 


[IMG]


Here $N_{a} =$ Anti bonding electron $=$ 4 and $N_{b} = 10$

(3) $\, ~$ After 14  electrons to 20 electrons molecular orbital configuration is - - -


[IMG]


Here $N_{a} = 10$

and $N_{b} = 10$

In O atom 8 electrons present, so in $O_{2},  8$ $\times$ 2 = 16 electrons present. 

in $O_{2}^{2-}$ no of electrons = 18

(A) Molecular orbital configuration of O ${}_{2}^{2-}$ (18 electrons) is 

$σ_{1s^{2}}σ_{1s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2s^{2}}σ_{2s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2p_{z}^{2}}π_{2p_{x}^{2}}=π_{2p_{y}^{2}}π_{2p_{x}^{2}}^{\ast }=π_{2p_{y}^{2}}^{\ast }$

$\therefore \quad$ $N_{b} = 10$

$N_{a} = 8$

$\therefore \quad$ BO = $\frac{1}{2}$ [ 10 $-$ 8] = 1

(B)   $C_{2}^{2-}$ has 14 electrons. 

Moleculer orbital configuration of $C_{2}^{2-}$ is

 $σ_{1s^{2}}σ_{1s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2s^{2}}σ_{2s^{2}}^{\ast }π_{2p_{x}^{2}}=π_{2p_{y}^{2}}σ_{2p_{z}^{2}}$

$\therefore \quadN_{a} = 4$

$N_{b} = 10$

$\therefore \quad$ BO = $\frac{1}{2}[10-4]=3$

(C)   $N_{2}^{2-}$ has 16 electrons. 

Moleculer orbital configuration of $N_{2}^{2-}$ is

 $σ_{1s^{2}}σ_{1s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2s^{2}}σ_{2s^{2}}^{\ast }π_{2p_{x}^{2}}=π_{2p_{y}^{2}}σ_{2p_{z}^{2}}π_{2p_{x}^{1}}^{\ast }=π_{2p_{y}^{1}}^{\ast }$

$\therefore \quadN_{a} = 6$

$N_{b} = 10$

$\therefore \quad$ BO = $\frac{1}{2}[10-6]=2$

The correct order of bond orders of $C_{2}^{2-}$, $N_{2}^{2-}$ and $O_{2}^{2-}$

$O_{2}^{2-}$ < $N_{2}^{2-}$ < $C_{2}^{2-}$

For a first order reaction, the time required for completion of 90% reaction is 'x' times the half life of the reaction. The value of 'x' is

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

text: PCl$_{5}$ is well known, but NCl$_{5}$ is not. because,
options: nitrogen is less reactive than phosphorus.
nitrogen doesn't have d-orbitals in its valence shell.
catenation tendency is weaker in nitrogen than phosphorus.
size of phosphorus is larger than nitrogen.

text: Transition metal complex with highest value of crystal field splitting ($\Delta_{0}$) will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Crystal field splitting $(\Delta _{0})$ for octahedral complexes depends on oxidation state of the metal as well as to which transition series the metal belongs. For the same oxidation state, the crystal field splitting $(\Delta _{0})$ increases as we move from $3d\to 4d\to 5d$

$\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}$ and $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$ belong to $3d$ series, $\mathrm{Mo}^{3+}$ belongs to $4d$ series and $\mathrm{Os}^{3+}$ belongs to $5d$ series. 

Therefore crystal field splitting $(\Delta _{0})$ is highest for $[\mathrm{Os}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{6}]^{3+}$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Evening Shift

text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I : The presence of weaker $π$-bonds makes alkenes less stable than alkanes.

Statement II : The strength of the double bond is greater than that of carbon-carbon single bond.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The $π$-bond present in alkenes is weaker than $σ$ bond present in alkanes. That makes alkenes less stable than alkanes. Therefore, statement-I is correct.

Carbon-carbon double bond is stronger than Carbon-carbon single bond because more energy is required to break 1 sigma and 1 pi bond than to break 1 sigma bond only. Therefore, statement-II is also correct.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Evening Shift

text: The conversion of propan-1-ol to n-butylamine involves the sequential addition of reagents. The correct sequential order of reagents is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Propan-1-ol has three carbon atoms and n-butylamine has four, so one carbon is added as a nitrile group.

$\mathrm{SOCl}{}_{2}$ converts the alcohol into 1-chloropropane, KCN replaces Cl by CN to give butanenitrile, and $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}$/Ni or Na(Hg)/$\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{OH}$ reduces $-\mathrm{C}\equiv \mathrm{N}$ to $-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}$:

$\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{OH}{}^{\mathrm{SOCl}{}_{2}\qquad }\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}{}^{\mathrm{KCN}}\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CN}{}^{\mathrm{H}{}_{2}/\mathrm{Ni}\qquad }\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}$


[IMG]

Sequences (B) and (D) keep a three-carbon chain, and (C) has no step that reduces the nitrile to the amine.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text:
PCl$_{5}$ dissociates as

PCl$_{5}(g)$ $⇌$ PCl$_{3}(g) + Cl_{2}(g)$

5 moles of PCl$_{5}$ are placed in a 200 litre vessel which contains 2 moles of $N_{2}$ and is maintained at 600 K. The equilibrium pressure is 2.46 atm. The equilibrium constant $K_{p}$ for the dissociation of PCl$_{5}$ is $__________$ $\times$ $10^{-3}. ($nearest integer)

(Given : R  = 0.082 L atm $K^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$; Assume ideal gas behaviour)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Here 2 moles of $N_{2}$ also present that is why 2 moles always have to add in total mole calculation.

At equilibrium,

Pressure (P) = 2.46 atm

Volume (V) = 200 L

Temperature (T) = 600 K

$\therefore$ Applying ideal gas equation,

PV = nRT

$\Rightarrow$ 2.46 $\times$ 200 = (7 + x) $\times$ 0.082 $\times$ 600

$\Rightarrow$ x = 3

Now,

$K_{P}=\frac{P_{PCl3}\times P_{Cl2}}{P_{PCl5}}$

$=\frac{\left [\frac{3}{7+3}\times 2.46\right ]\left [\frac{3}{7+3}\times 2.46\right ]}{\left [\frac{5-3}{7+3}\times 2.46\right ]}$

$=\frac{\frac{3}{10}\times \frac{3}{10}\times (2.46)^{2}}{\frac{2}{10}\times 2.46}$

$=\frac{9}{20}\times 2.46$

$=1107\times 10^{-3}$ atm
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Evening Shift

text: The resistance of a conductivity cell containing 0.01 M KCl solution at 298 K is 1750 $\Omega$. If the conductivity of 0.01 M KCl solution at 298 K is 0.152 $\times$ $10^{-3} S cm^{-1}$, then the cell constant of the conductivity cell is $____________$ $\times$ $10^{-3} cm^{-1}$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Molarity of $\mathrm{KCl}$ solution $=0.01\mathrm{M}$

$\begin{array}{ll} \text{Resistance} & =1750\mathrm{ohm} \\  \\ \text{Conductivity} & =0.152\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{S}\mathrm{cm}^{-1} \\  \\ \text{Conductivity} & =\frac{\text{Cell constant}}{\text{Resistance}} \\  \\ \therefore \text{Cell constant} & =0.152\times 10^{-3}\times 1750 \\  \\  & =266\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{cm}^{-1} \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Evening Shift
